latest_apis.rationale: The stack is genuinely current: Angular 22.2, zoneless by default with no zone.js dep, OnPush + signals everywhere, signal inputs, built-in control flow, and strict mode/strictTemplates via the v22 scaffold defaults (angular-cli#32993, angular#67802). The one systematic gap is data loading: every fetch goes through hand-built RxJS switchMap/shareReplay chains bridged with toSignal, when v22 just promoted resource/httpResource to stable as the recommended async primitive (v22 release blog, PR angular#68253). Routes are also all eagerly bundled contrary to the framework's lazy-loading recommendation.

Deductions: the #moves anchor jump is a hand-rolled timing hack duplicating a router feature, and the static server re-declares a MIME map (defensible for zero extra deps).

churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is well-fenced behind ApiService/CatalogService and models, so an API change touches few files, and nothing relies on framework internals. But the alternate-form rule and the document-title rule are copy-pasted across pages instead of being one constant or a custom router TitleStrategy, so the next requirement tweak ripples.

findings.issue: All data loading is hand-composed RxJS (switchMap/forkJoin/shareReplay) bridged to signals via toSignal, even though resource/rxResource/httpResource became stable in Angular 22 as the recommended async primitive; the pipelines manually manage caching and get no request cancellation or status signal.
findings.suggestion: Rebuild the per-page fetch chains (species → pokemon → moves-per-game) with rxResource/httpResource keyed on a route-param signal; keep the ApiService cache for shared catalog data.

findings.issue: Anchor scrolling to #moves is hand-rolled with an effect, window.location.hash and setTimeout, duplicating the router's built-in behavior and relying on undocumented timing.
findings.suggestion: Provide the router with withInMemoryScrolling({ anchorScrolling: 'enabled' }) (or the v22 platform Navigation API option) and delete the effect.

findings.issue: Every page component is eagerly imported, so the whole app ships in the initial bundle, contrary to the Angular loading-strategy guidance (lazy-load everything except the landing page).
findings.suggestion: Use loadComponent: () => import(...) for the five non-home routes to split per-page chunks.

findings.issue: The alternate-form cutoff (id > 10000) is a magic number duplicated in catalog.service.ts:100, move-page.ts:70, type-page.ts:73 and ability-page.ts:63.
findings.suggestion: Extract one isDefaultForm(id) helper (next to idFromUrl in core/format.ts) so the exclusion rule lives in one place.

findings.issue: The '<h1> – Pokédex' title rule is re-implemented as a per-page effect+Title.setTitle copy-paste in five components (move-page.ts:83, ability-page.ts:76, type-page.ts:93, not-found-page.ts:15, home-page.ts:115).
findings.suggestion: Implement a custom TitleStrategy for provideRouter so the rule is configured once.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but no form directive or API is used anywhere in src.
findings.suggestion: Remove it from dependencies; the native controls in home-page.html and pokemon-page.html don't need it.

findings.issue: queryParamMap values are coerced with `params as unknown as Map<string,string>`, discarding the router's actual ParamMap type.
findings.suggestion: Type parseQuery against ParamMap (or bind q/type/generation/page as component inputs via withComponentInputBinding) and drop the cast.

findings.issue: provideHttpClient() with no features is redundant in Angular 21+: HttpClient is injectable by default and uses the fetch backend; the no-arg call only re-registers the default feature set.
findings.suggestion: Delete the provider (or keep it only if interceptors/XSRF configuration is added later).

findings.issue: Mixed naming generations: pages follow the v20+ suffixless convention (home-page.ts/HomePage) while services use pre-v20 filenames (api.service.ts, catalog.service.ts) and two shared classes keep the old Component suffix (PokemonCardComponent, NotFoundComponent).
findings.suggestion: Align on one convention, e.g. core/api.ts and class PokemonCard, per the v20+ 'intent over role' style guide.

findings.issue: The sprite fallback subscribes imperatively inside an event handler with no teardown or cancellation (and `track $index` on sortable rows at pokemon-page.html:125 causes needless DOM churn on every sort).
findings.suggestion: Expose the fallback via a computed/httpResource-derived URL instead of a fire-and-forget subscription, and track sortable rows by a stable key (move name + level).

summary: This is a genuinely current Angular 22 codebase: zoneless by default, signals and OnPush everywhere, signal inputs, built-in control flow, strict mode via the new v22 scaffold defaults, and a dependency list that is exactly the CLI minimum. The forward-thinking gaps are concentrated in data loading — RxJS plumbing where v22's newly stable resource/httpResource would give cancellation, status and less boilerplate — plus eager route bundles and a few copy-pasted rules (title, alternate-form cutoff, hand-rolled anchor scrolling). Aging risk is moderate and localized: an upgrade would touch few files, mostly the core services and route config.

apis.replacement: redundant since v21 — HttpClient is injectable by default with the fetch backend
v22 introduces @Service() as the preferred shorthand; @Injectable is not deprecated
stable resource/rxResource/httpResource (Angular 22) is now the recommended way to bring async data into signals
httpResource/resource would provide built-in status, abort and reload semantics
